subtopics.title: The Adjustments That Make the Year True

questions.question: The year's total depreciation is:
options: R12 200 — vehicle R60 000 straight-line at 15% gives R9 000; equipment at 20% of the carrying value R16 000 gives R3 200

questions.question: Telephone paid R3 300 with February's R300 account unpaid means:
options: Expense becomes R3 600, and the R300 accrued expense stands as a current liability
The R300 is next year's expense

questions.question: Insurance paid R2 400 including R400 for next year means:
options: Expense R2 000, with the R400 prepaid expense standing as a current asset

questions.question: Rent income received R8 800 at R800 a month, one month outstanding, means:
options: Income becomes R9 600, with the R800 accrued income standing as a current asset

subtopics.title: From Final Accounts to the Two Statements

questions.question: The trading account shows:
options: Sales R150 000 less cost of sales R100 000 — gross profit R50 000, confirming the 50% mark-up on cost

questions.question: Net profit for the year is:
options: R19 800 — gross profit 50 000 plus rent income 9 600 minus operating expenses 39 800

questions.question: Owner's equity at year-end is:
options: R100 400 — opening 88 000 plus profit 19 800 less drawings 7 400

questions.question: The statement of financial position balances at:
options: R110 000 — non-current assets 90 800 plus current assets 19 200, against equity 100 400 plus current liabilities 9 600

questions.question: Gross profit on cost of 50% tells the reader that:
options: The achieved margin equals the mark-up policy exactly — so no stock leaked away unrecorded

questions.question: The current ratio of 2 : 1 means:
options: Two rand of current assets stand ready for every rand of current liabilities — comfortable liquidity
Stock turns over twice a year

questions.question: The acid test of just over 1 : 1 (9 700 over 9 600) shows:
options: The business cannot pay without borrowing
Even without selling a single item, the immediate debts can be covered — sound, worth keeping there

questions.question: Return on equity of 21% is judged by comparing it to:
options: What a bank pays on savings — several times better here, the reward for effort and risk

subtopics.title: Guards, Rules and the Cost of One Unit

questions.question: Division of duties as an internal control means:
options: The one who records the money is not the one who banks it — no hand touches money end to end
Every worker does every job in turn

questions.question: Prudence, as a GAAP principle, requires:
options: Treating the owner and business as one person

questions.question: The candles' unit cost is:
options: R15 — prime cost 6 000 (materials 3 500 plus labour 2 500) plus overheads 1 500, over 500 units

questions.question: The budget skeleton for next month closes at:
options: R4 000 — receipts 11 000, payments 8 500, surplus 2 500, plus the opening balance of 1 500

subtopics.title: Tidying the Room Before the Photo

questions.question: Year-end as "photo day" means:
options: One picture of the business at midnight on the last day, tidied so outsiders can trust it
The premises are photographed for insurance
The statements are printed in colour
Stock is photographed instead of counted

questions.question: The four tidying movements are:
options: All pushes — everything moves to next year
Depreciation admitted; the owed phone account pulled in; next year's insurance pushed out; the earned rent pulled in

questions.question: An untidied photo "flatters or slanders" because:
options: Skipping depreciation makes the business look richer than it is; skipping owed expenses makes costs look smaller than they were
Tidying changes the profit to whatever the owner wants

subtopics.title: The Report Card and the Health Check

questions.question: The report card's three floors are:
options: The trading result R50 000; plus the tenant's rent R9 600; less the running costs R39 800 — the year's true mark R19 800

questions.question: The health check differs from the report card in that:
options: It asks how the body is DOING underneath the mark — liquidity, solvency and return, each judged by a comparison
Only the bank may read it

questions.question: "Numbers alone say nothing; numbers COMPARED say everything" gives the comment recipe:
options: Here is the figure, here is what I compared it to, here is my judgement
Repeat the question in the answer

subtopics.title: Locks on the Doors, and What One Candle Costs

questions.question: The tuck shop where one person takes, counts, records and banks the money is:
options: Not a system but an invitation — no division of duties, nothing forcing errors or theft into the open
Acceptable if the person is family

questions.question: The classic repairs for it are:
options: Split the jobs; a numbered slip for every movement; a second nod before paying; stock counted by someone who does not sell it
Bank the cash weekly instead of daily

questions.question: One candle costs:
options: R15 — wax and wicks 3 500, hands 2 500, table and burner 1 500: R7 500 over 500 candles; at R20 each carries R5 home

questions.question: The year's three street laws are:
options: Buy low, sell high, bank often
Guard the money with split hands and slips; know what one unit truly costs; write the month before living it
